utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Mr. Registrar, can you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, and good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the appearances, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis and Laurie Sartorio, assisted by our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to my learned friends from the OTP. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas Robson for Mr. Delic. Our case manager is Ms. Lejla Gluhic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Good morning, sir. How are you this morning? Let me just warn you that, at the beginning of your testimony, you made a declaration to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth, and I just want to warn you that you are still bound by that declaration. Okay?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Imamovic. I was asking you some questions concerning the incidents regarding the Mujahedin. This is something that you reported on at the time. I have several questions left about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show the witness Exhibit 576.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you remember seeing this document, don't you, just before the weekend? The OTP showed you this document. It was produced by the 35th Division, dated the 25th of May, 1995, sent to the Command of the 3rd Corps, the Security Service. It bears your name, and you claim that you signed the document. You remember that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You explained that in this document, you forwarded some evidence to the Security Department of the 3rd Corps; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also explained that this is in relation to a particular incident which involved the pressing of charges against someone; right? You remember that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember if charges were eventually pressed or not. I can't say either way, but I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. More about that. You were testifying on the 11th of October, 2007; 3964 is the transcript page, lines 18 through 29. You were asked the following question by the OTP: Do you know whether any response was provided to that letter you wrote or the attachment; in other words, was an investigation launched? I want you to clarify to the Trial Chamber the following: It's true, isn't it, that you, as the security organ in the 35th Division, when you recorded an incident like that, the desecration of the cemetery, you were actually responsible for launching an investigation, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the military police that was responsible for launching an investigation, and I believe one of my associates was actually working with the military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Be that as it may, it was the military police of your Command that conducted this investigation or was it actually a lower-ranking command; the brigade, for example?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say for sure, but, as always, everyone was involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You took photographs of the cemetery and you produced an official note of the security organ. You forwarded all of this material to your superior command, did you not?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely what this document speaks about.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that, at the very end, it says: "Operative work on the case is ongoing. We shall keep you up to date." That is the last sentence of the document, is it not?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, in other words, you are here reporting that the investigation is bound to continue; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we can now put this document away. Could the witness now please look at Exhibit 577.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, it wasn't necessary for your superior command to necessarily do something about a document like this, since the investigation was still underway, and I mean the document that we just saw a while ago, not the new one that has just come up?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One needs to wait for the conclusion of an investigation before one does anything about it. Before that stage, it is not necessary for superiors to do anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Have you this new document in front of you. I believe you've seen it already, and this is a document produced by your organ. You were shown this by the Prosecutor as well. It is a document produced by the Security Service of the 35th Division, and this is about members of the 328th Brigade and the 4th Battalion transferring to the El Mudjahedin Detachment. You see that, don't you? You remember the document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: First and foremost, Witness --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- or rather, could the witness be shown page 2 of this document first? It's the last page of the English text with the signature, or where the signature should be. Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You realise that your name is there. Where the signature should be, we see your name. It says: "Certified by stamp and signature." You agree that we can't find your actual initials on this page, can we?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, we can't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could please go back to the first page of this document now. Let's zoom in on the upper half of the page. The same applies to the English. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you please, once again, clarify the following: You said this document was encrypted and dispatched by packet communications; right? You remember that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You see the first portion of the document. There's a line, and please look closely at what it says above the line. You were the one forwarding quite a number of documents that were encrypted because you were a security officer, and I have the following question for you for that reason: Am I right if I say that encrypted documents were dispatched in the following way: Whoever is in charge of manning and operating the packet communications equipment receives the original documents to be dispatched, right, the document that is to be sent to someone? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The next thing is this: The document is copied or typed up, if you like, so that the recipient receives a typed-up version of the original text, this being the reason why the stamp and signature cannot be seen on the document that the recipient eventually gets; am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If we want to see the original, then we have to go to the top of the document, the file number or the file name and the number, right, and these two references will help us track down the original document, in a manner of speaking? We need a file name in order to find that, don't we?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are references that tell us what file we are looking for, what document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. You see what it says there: "Certified by stamp and signature." By no means does this mean that the signature in question is yours. "Certified by stamp and signature," generically speaking, it could have been anyone's signature, couldn't it? I don't mean necessarily anyone outside the Security Service. I mean someone else who was part of the Security Service who would have been authorised to sign on your behalf. Right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had a number of associates who were authorised to sign these documents off, and a number of other documents show just that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, if we want to know for sure who signed a particular document, we have to go to the original to make sure; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask you about this particular document. There's something else I want to ask you. You agree that it talks about members of the 328th Brigade and the 4th Battalion being transferred to the El Mudjahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would say willful abandonment of their own unit, unauthorised departure from their own unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. You informed your superior command about this, and the Prosecutor asked you questions to this effect: "Did the superior command do anything with that at all document?" You remember being asked that question, don't you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For that reason, I want you to look at PP2373. 2373.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, can you please confirm that this is an order by the 3rd Corps, dated the 9th of August, 1995, and the title is "Order Being Returned to the El Mudjahedin Detachment"?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at the introduction, if that can be zoomed in on, please, just for us to see the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: For whatever reason, the number is crossed out. It says: "Pursuant to a report from the Military Security Service, strictly confidential number," and we can't see the number, can we; and then it goes on to say this: "As of the 6th of August, 1995." You remember that the document a while ago bore the date the 6th of August?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please have a look: The El Mudjahedin Detachment is hereby being ordered to immediately return the persons they received into their unit without appropriate transfer orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, I don't know what is written on the B/C/S; but on the English, this document refers to a document written on the 4th of August, not the 6th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is an obvious translation error. In the Bosnian, we see this reference to the 6th of August, if you could please just zoom in the relevant portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I can see the "6th of August" in the B/C/S. Thank you so much. I see also that part of the sentence just before the date in the B/C/S has been blocked out.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is a PT document of the Prosecution. They probably got it like this from their archive, and this is the form in which it was eventually submitted to us by the OTP. I suppose this is how they got it, to begin with. The Defence got what you see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you agree with me that, obviously, the 3rd Corps Command is here trying to deal with problems trying to place this unit within the command system, I mean the El Mujahid Detachment, and to forestall any willful action on their part?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 590.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now D548. For the record, this is a document of the 3rd Corps Security Service or Security Department, the 22nd of April, 1995, and it's about the El Mudjahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I believe, Witness, that you have never set eyes on this document; however, you testified that in this period of time, the detachment was in your area. It is for that reason that I wish to ask you this. Can you please just go through the document? It's a very brief document. This is a security document, and I believe you're familiar with its substance. I want to ask you something about that. The Security Department of the 3rd Corps Command, that was your superior command, was it not?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a member of the Military Security Department, you knew that there was an order to stop drafting soldiers into the El Mudjahedin Detachment, and it took effect on the 22nd of April, 1995, at the very latest. Did you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but I'm sure that the last document was about soldiers taking action without appropriate authorisation and joining that unit without appropriate authorisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "the previous document," you mean that other people joined this unit from other units, so this constituted a violation of the document that you now have in front of you; right? So you do allow for the possibility that you knew about this ban on joining the El Mujahedin unit, or rather, the El Mudjahedin Detachment being forbidden from the receiving of these soldiers into their rank, and that it took effect on the 22nd of April, 1995, at the latest?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have known. I do allow for the possibility, but I don't for this particular document. The report by the Security Service of the 35th Division must have been a consequence of this document, among other things.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 591.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit 575 now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, for the record, Witness, this is a daily report by the Military Security Service of the 35th Division, is it not? The date is the 18th of August, 1995. This is a document that you were shown by the OTP during your testimony. You remember that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please zoom in on the lower half of the page, Your Honours, so that the witness can jog his memory.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were shown this last paragraph by the OTP. It was about psychological training. This is the next page in English. You remember that you looked at this document, talking about the psychological training of the 328th Mountain Brigade, the 3rd and 4th Battalions, with the El Mudjahedin Detachment. You remember looking at this document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we put this one away now, because I want the witness to look at a different document now in connection with this one. Could the witness now please be shown P571 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Ms. Vidovic, could you please repeat the number?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D571. This is a document produced by the 3rd Corps Military Security Department, the 10th of September, 1995. It was sent to the Security Administration of the BH Army General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Again, this is a document produced by your superior command, is it not?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please now go to page 2, which is page 3 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, about midway down the page, it reads: "We are in possession of reliable information that," and there is a reference to the 4th Battalion then. Midway down in the English, it says: "We are in possession ..." You see that, Witness? Can you please read that paragraph to yourself? You can see the reference to the El Mudjahedin Detachment there, can't you? Witness, the reference is here to the 3rd and 4th Manoeuvre Battalions. There was a reference to those in our previous documents a while ago, wasn't there? They were receiving psychological training at the hands of the El Mudjahedin Detachment; right? There is reference here to the 328th Brigade and these two battalions. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that or do you agree that this document describes the satisfaction on the part of the members of the 3rd and 4th Battalions because of the way the El Mudjahedin Detachment treated the BH flag? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Further, there's a reference there to the fact that certain individuals from the El Mudjahedin Detachment claimed before the soldiers that this wasn't their flag, and that it should therefore be burned. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It goes on to say that they have no confidence in the army's leadership and soldiers, and they, on the other hand, had to be trusted. Have you heard of incidents such as these? Since this is a Security Department document, you might be familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is something that we reported at the time to our superior organ. The training of BH Army soldiers, alongside with the El Mudjahedin Detachment soldiers, was organised in order to develop a feeling of mutual trust; however, it turned out that because there were things like these going on, precisely what's reported here, that what was eventually achieved was quite the contrary, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this document reflect the real situation, as far as confidence in the army's leadership was concerned and also the way the flag was treated by the El Mudjahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm certain of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a number for this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 592.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now on to a different topic. I hope you can help us with it, too. Would you agree with me that Zavidovici was a peculiar area during the war because it remained isolated from the corps commander for a long time and from the Supreme Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because Zavidovici was, to all practical intents, in the crossfire between the Republika Srpska Army, on the one hand, and the BH Army, on the other, and then the Washington Agreement was signed in February 1994. So, on the other side, there was the HVO, not the BH Army. So Zavidovici remained under siege for quite a long time. It was a sealed-off area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Isolated from the rest of the BH Army, to a large extent; would that be a fair assessment?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Under those circumstances, it was very difficult to exercise command over the army unit. It was very difficult to provide the logistics and everything else that combat under those circumstances would have required.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that, under the circumstances, the civilian authorities and the religious leaders had a powerful impact on life in the area, in general, and the way the defence was organised, right, in Zavidovici?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I had a chance to see this for myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you accept that the relations between the Mujahedin and the civilian authorities in the Zavidovici area were much closer than the relations between the El Mujahedin and the military authorities?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This could be concluded on the basis of different events, in particular in view of the fact that the majority of the civilians joined the El Mujahedin unit of their own volition.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can Exhibit number 509 be shown to the witness, please, at this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is the Security Department of the 3rd Corps memo from the 12th of August, 1995, which speaks about the relations in the zone of the 35 Division of the KoV, of the land forces. This is again a document of your superior command, is it not, Mr. Imamovic?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a document of the Security Service of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this information from the field was received by the Security Service of the 3rd Corps, from the department, from the section in which you also worked; that is to say, from the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This describes precisely the relations that I spoke about in my previous answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. So please be so kind as to go through this document. I can see that you are looking at it. Look at this particular part, where reference is made to the El Mujahedin unit and the Asim Camdzic unit, and I shall quote. It says: "In SDA speeches of individuals at religious gatherings, they belittled the results of the army and glorified the results of the Asim Camdzic unit and the El Mujahedin unit, which caused mistrust among the civilians, among the citizens, in the Command of the Army." You are aware of these events, are you not? Does this document actually reflect the actual situation in the field, in August 1995, that is?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So speeches of this kind by individuals, like the sentence that I have just read out for you, were in fact support by the civilian authorities to these units, were they not -- was it not?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this document can now be put away, but I should like to show another document in connection with this. This is document D572. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, I'm going to ask you first to take a look at the signature at the end of this document. Do you recognise this signature?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So this is the signature of the commander, Colonel Fadil Hasanagic, is it not?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you scroll down the document, please, so that we can take a look at it. Yes, that is okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, is this a document of the 19th of July, 1995, which is an information sent to the Chief of Zavidovici Municipality, to the Chief of the Public Security Service of Zavidovici, as well as to the Executive Committee of the Party of Democratic Action of Zavidovici? The SDA actually stands for the Party of Democratic Action, does it not, Witness?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the highest organ of the Democratic -- Party of Democratic Action in Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, Witness, try to go through this document. It is not very long, and I should then like to ask you a number of questions. Do you agree that, by this document, Colonel Hasanagic addresses the civilian authorities and informs them about excesses being committed by the Asim Camdzic and El Mujahedin units; am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It seems that you, in the Division - and I'm referring actually to the Division Command - that you were aware of these problems with the El Mujahid unit and the other unit, the Asim Camdzic, and of the fact that these problems could be handled by civilian authorities, and that is why the colonel is addressing the civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were aware of that, but this is the only time, the only instance when we actually addressed the civilian authorities on account of those problems, for here it is stated at the end of the document that those who are responsible for public law and order in the city, or rather, throughout the municipality, that it was high time that they took measures in order to put an end to such incidents.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Would I be right to say that the Division expected a solution from the political structures and from the Zavidovici Municipality leadership? That is what appears to be the case on the basis of this document.

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because we understood when we realised that they had a much greater influence on the unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 593.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you will agree with me, will you not, that it would not be usual in the command structure, in the command-and-control structure, for the commander of, for instance, a division to inform the civilian authorities of the problems that he has with his subordinates. He would deal with them himself or within the chain of command and control, would he not?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a unique case in military practice.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mrs. Vidovic, I have a question. Is the document that we saw which refers to the report, to the relationships between the members of the El Mudjahedin Detachment and civilian population, or is it a document that deals with the members of this detachment and their relationship with members of the Bosnian Army and the structure of command of the Army? Could you possibly clarify this aspect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not quite sure I understood you well. The relation between the El Mujahedin and the command structures, or the relation between the El Mujahid unit and the civilian structures?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is precisely what I'm trying to understand. I want to know what this document deals with, exactly. My feeling was that the colonel was referring or addressing the civilian authorities in order for them to resolve the problems that members of the El Mudjahedin Detachment were provoking within the civilian population. Then, again, I may be mistaken, but I didn't think it was about problems within the army. I thought it was problems within the civilian population; therefore, he addresses civilian authorities. Am I mistaken? Do I make a wrong interpretation of this document or am I right in my assumption?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In view of the fact that these were incidents that, as far as I could understand, were within the domain of disturbances of the public law and order, by members of the El Mudjahedin Detachment, that is why the commander of the 35th Division called upon the civilian structures, both political and primarily the civilian police, because this fell within their ambit of work; that is, the prevention of disturbances of public law and order. He called upon them to take an active part in suppressing this, to put a definite end to such things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... was impotent to do anything about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. We didn't hear what was impotent to do anything about that. Can you repeat that, please? Who was impotent or what was impotent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The commander of the 35th Division was in no position to use the military police in order to prevent such incidents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed, but it's not a question of he was in no position; it was a question of it was not in his area of responsibility. This is a civilian problem, isn't it? You have just explained that. It didn't fall within his responsibility within the military?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, just one question in connection with your previous answer: If you were, and you were a member of the 35th Division, if you were, if you committed, that is to say, any offences vis a vis the population as an individual, you would have fallen under military authority or had been subject to action by military court, irrespective of the fact that your actions targeted civilians; am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what to say. Certainly, I would have been taken to account, I would have borne some consequences, I would have answered to both civil and military authorities for that conduct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please. When members of a regular army unit engage in excesses of any kind, for instance, they burglarise a store, they would have to answer according to military regulations of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That would be a breach of military discipline.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's just it. So the fact that Hasanagic is addressing the civilian authorities, turning to the civilian authorities because the El Mujahedin unit is disturbing the public law and order, actually attests to the fact that he is unable to control them within the chain of command and is unable to take measures to stop them?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I shall now move to a different topic that you have testified about, and that is prisoners of war. In making your statement about prisoners of war, you accepted that the procedure with POWs was a prescribed one and that these regulations -- that people in the field were familiar with these regulations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you a number of documents demonstrating that you were in touch with a number of prisoners held by the -- by members of the El Mujahedin unit; and in your testimony, you described a brief encounter them. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I shall just like the witness to take a brief look at Exhibit 553. And until the document appears, for the record, this is a document of a section of the Security Service of the 35th Division from the 22nd of July, 1995, and it is entitled "Report on Talk with POWs.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in testifying about this document, you said that you had a very brief interview with these prisoners on the 22nd of July, 1995; is that correct? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document be put away now. Can the witness be shown Exhibit number 582 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You will recall having seen this bulletin during your testimony,.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please scroll the document down so the number of the bulletin can be seen, which is number 137, and the date it bears, which is the 22nd of July, 1995. Can page 4, i.e., page 5 of the English version, be shown to the witness, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at part of this midway paragraph. You remember that the Prosecutor also drew your attention to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, it is the previous page in the English version. This is the document, actually, the paragraph, Your Honours, which starts with the words: "The 3rd Corps," i.e., the SVB of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you see it being stated here that 50 aggressor soldiers have been liquidated and about 40 taken prisoners, among whom two were doctors and one nurse? I should like to ask you, in connection with this: Do you agree that this figure of 40 prisoners is, in fact, exaggerated, and that you actually never heard of so large a number being taken -- having been taken prisoner by the El Mujahedin unit in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never heard that. Actually, I was surprised when I saw this document. Both the number of the liquidated people and the number of people taken prisoners were surprising. I don't know that it was that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the figures about killed soldiers and soldiers taken prisoners by a brigade would be sometimes blown up in order to actually enhance the successes of the individual units, brigades?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. False reporting was a problem that we had at the time; false reporting on combat operations undertaken, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you did report such problems to your superior command, did you not?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did, as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a closer look at the last sentence, where it says: "All the aggressor soldiers taken prisoner are being kept by the El Mujahid unit, who for now will not allow access to them." Please take a mental note of that sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we see that in the English version?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It is on the following page. I apologise, Your Honours. It is there now. Your Honours, may I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown Exhibit number 581.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You'll see, Witness, this is also an information by the 3rd Corps Military Security Service, sent to the General Staff Security Administration on the 23rd of July, 1995, and it refers to the aggressor soldiers. You will remember this document having also been shown to you by the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you remember -- do you remember that you said that this was an information which was drawn up by you, or rather, it was just copied by the 3rd Corps, and then sent on, forwarded on?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I said. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can see the names "Branko Sikanic, Igor Guljevatej," and "Sikanic." So this is information sent on the 23rd of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the document be scrolled down so we can see the stamp, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can see this is a signature of Colonel Ekrem Alihodzic. Witness, please take --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- or rather, can we scroll down this document so that the witness can see the number of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please remember the number of this document, which is 03/1-163-292-1. Please remember that number.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Can the witness now take a look at document D573.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, a while ago, I drew your attention to this number; right? First of all, do you agree this is a document produced by the Military Security Administration the 26th of July, 1995, signed by General Jusuf Jasarevic? You agree with all of this; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You do know who he is, the Brigadier-General Jusuf Jasarevic? You knew of him at the time, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree the document bears the following title "Interview with Prisoners, Instruction"? You agree; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, look at this. In reference to your Document Number 03/1-163-292-1, the 23rd of July, 1995, this is the number that I told you about a while ago. It's the same number, isn't it? "Information by the Security Service of the 3rd Corps." This is a brief document. I see that you've read it. Do you agree that this document is providing instructions that interviews should be conducted with prisoners and that the Military Security Administration of the General Staff should be informed about the results; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you agree that the General Staff Administration reacted immediately upon receiving this information on prisoners, received from the 3rd Corps? A set of instructions came a mere two or three days later?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're quite right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, before we leave this document, I'd like the witness to explain to us: What is General Jasarevic asking here? Apparently, he's asking to conduct detailed IR/informative interviews and to inform the SVB Military Security Service about this. What is an "IR/informative interview"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Interview for the purposes of obtaining information. This is an interview normally conducted by a security officer from the Intelligence Department. They interview a POW. They ask them about their personal details, which unit they belong to, the circumstances of their capture; and among other things, this is also about how POWs are treated during their captivity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: That's what I thought. So this instruction was addressed to the 3rd Corps. Do you recall having seen this instruction being forwarded from the 3rd Corps to the 35th Division; that is to say, to your office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't, not specifically, but I assume that this interview was conducted by members of the Military Security Service and the Intelligence Service of the 3rd Corps. This is merely an assumption on my part, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Why would the 3rd Corps suddenly intervene in this? I mean, the original information about the detained POWs came from the 35th Division and was transmitted through the 3rd Corps to the General Staff. Now, the General Staff then writes back and says, "Please make sure that these people are being properly interviewed, including interviewed about their state of health." This instruction then goes back to the 3rd Corps but, apparently, is never passed on to the 35th Division, and my question is: Why not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So, for that reason, also, you would have no way of knowing whether these interviews were actually ever carried out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the following document may assist us -- or rather, can we please have a number for this document first?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we please just let you know first that you're ten minutes beyond the time taken by the Prosecution. I just want to know how long it will take you to finish with this witness. The document is admitted into evidence. May we please have an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 594.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, how far are you?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, between ten and 15 minutes, certainly not more, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Proceed, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. Could the witness please be shown PT2447, PT2447. It's a mistake in the transcript, 2447.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, this is a report by the Military Security Service of the 3rd Corps, dated the 25th of July, 1995. This is entitled "Results of Interviews with Captured Aggressor Soldiers." I would now like you to look at these names: "Branko Sikanic, Velibor Trivicevic, Igor Guljevatej." Before we move on to the next page, if you could please try and explain, just above these names, it reads: "Security organ of the Military Security Service of the 35th Division, while interviewing captured aggressor soldiers, obtained the following information." You see the date there, the 25th of July; right? So this is a new interview in relation to the one that you mentioned that occurred on the 22nd of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please pull the document up a little.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please look at this, the next page in English. Could you please look at this, and, again, it says: "Based on such interviews as were conducted by the security organ of the 35th Division, the following information was obtained."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if we could please turn the page in the electronic version, in the B/C/S as well and the English, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Look at this page now, Witness, please. Will you agree with me that there is a whole sequence of details being described here, details that were discussed with these prisoners? Do you agree that there is some information here concerning enemy units and various aspects of their activity?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see the next page, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you seen any references at all to the El Mudjahedin Detachment? Would you not agree with me that it, indeed, appears that the 35th Division conducted a detailed interview with these prisoners, and as a result forwarded a report to the 3rd Corps on this? Was it you, was it someone else, and do you remember an interview like that being conducted with these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this particular interview at all. I certainly wasn't the one who conducted it, and I'm not sure if anyone else did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that there is not a single reference to the El Mudjahedin Detachment in this document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I notice that word being used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, if you look in the English at page 4, the paragraph, the topmost paragraph as appears now, it says: "The Battalion Commander escaped by stealing a medical vehicle and leaving us with six wounded to be captured by the Mujahedin and the Army." There is a reference to Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Your Honour, quite true.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is something that one of the prisoners is telling us; right? It's a story by --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not asking for your interpretation. I'm just saying there is a reference to Mujahedin. That's what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, there is reference there to Mujahedin and not to the detachment itself; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. My question to you now: This document does not in any way suggest that the El Mudjahedin Detachment was now banning anyone from accessing prisoners. This document doesn't even tell us that these prisoners are still in the hand of El Mudjahedin Detachment. Is there a single reference to anything like that at all in this document, Witness?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not to the extent that I've been able to read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if we could just go to the last page in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam, after that page, will it be convenient to go for a break?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, oh, my apologies, Your Honours. Thank you very much, indeed. All right, we'll press on. This is an important document, or at least that's what I believe. My apologies there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll take a break and we'll come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we have a number for the document that we looked at before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, Exhibit number 594.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I think we already had 594.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We already had 594, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise, 595.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. D435 is our next document. This is my last document, and I have several questions about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the English comes up, for the record, do you agree this is a document produced by the 35th Division. It was produced in Zavidovici on the 17th of August, 1995, and the title is: "The Situation concerning Combat Readiness of the Command and Units of the 35th Division, KoV."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have a look at the next page, please, the last page of the document, the signature? It is the last page of the English, as well. We see a name there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, this is your name, isn't it? You saw the first page of the document, too. Based on what you've seen, is this a document that you produced?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we please go back to page 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you please focus on paragraph 2. It says: "Having analysed developments in the area of responsibility of the 328th Brigade." Can you please read that. I will give you some time to read that to yourself. It seems, Witness, doesn't it, based on this document, that you looked into the situation prevailing in the 328th Brigade, did you not?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From the security aspect, the brigade posed a problem for you, at least that's what the present document seems to indicate, does it not?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It seems that in paragraph 2 of the document, you concluded, having analysed the development on the 17th of August, 1995, that the command and control -- the chain of command and control in this brigade had failed completely; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We established that there were certain problems, and that would seem to be the inference, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You grow on to write there is no control on how any measures ordered are being implemented in this brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You go on to state that there are severe problems concerning false reporting. Is this what you were talking about a while ago during your evidence, the problem of false reporting?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You go on to state that certain officers appointed to important establishment posts do not meet even the bear minimum of moral and technical requirements?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was one of the problems we are facing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: These appointments were effected directly by politicians, were they not, appointments to the 328th Brigade; would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Their influence over the command-and-control system was quite obvious. An example such as the ones mentioned in my report, they clearly indicate that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this document reflect what the relations were and what the situation was in the area covered by the units of the 35th Division? You made this analysis based on facts; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You state here that the 35th Division Command is obviously divided. Was that a fact?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were divisions, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have page 2 for the benefit of the Chamber, please; page 2 of the English, page 2 of the B/C/S as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On this page, you go on to describe the internal relations within the Division. Have a look, please. You say that the Chief of Staff never went to meetings, that's all, the meetings at the Command. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were certain time periods when the Chief of Staff had no communication with the others. Mostly, he communicated with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, what does "RIK" stand for, sir? On the previous page, there's an abbreviation called "RIK."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Control and command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 596.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic. Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Just a couple of questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'd like to refer back to the document that was shown to you by Defence counsel of the 19th of July of 1995, where Colonel Hasanagic wrote to the Chief of the Zavidovici Municipality regarding the public security situation. Are you aware of any time where the -- when the SJB were subordinated to the military?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we please get to know what the "SJB" is?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: It's on the document, Your Honour. It's the "Public Security Station" in the town of Zavidovici. I don't believe this document was admitted in evidence, and I apologise, I don't know if the Defence, my learned colleague, could assist me in getting the"D" number, so we could bring the document back up. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document of the 19th of July?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that D572? D572 is Exhibit 593.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, 593. Could we -- that's the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you recall that document, sir, or would you like to see it again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please recall it on the screen, Madam, and let the witness see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. Can the witness be shown Exhibit 593. Okay. I'll repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: My question, sir, is: Were you aware or are you aware of any time when the SJB, the Public Security Station, was subordinated to the ARBiH in 1995?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, the civilian police was a component of the BH armed forces. Exceptionally, it could be used in dangerous situations, or rather, in combat operations. It was at such times that it was subordinated to the army commands and units. As for upholding public order, it was not specifically subordinated to any local army commands.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. This document may be put away.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, you were also asked by Defence counsel, at line 15 -- page 15, line 16, there was a reference to the SDA party and speeches that were given. Do you recall that document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to have a look, if it's no trouble.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. If we could go back to, excuse me, line 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think it's 509, just to speed things up.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I appreciate that. May the witness be shown that exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you recall being asked some questions about this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a while ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, could you tell us who at that time was the overall leader of the SDA or the Party for Democratic Action?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me just get when you say "overall leader," do you recall a national leader or a leader in Zavidovici?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The national leader.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The national leader. Who was the national leader of the SDA at the time, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Alija Izetbegovic was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Imamovic, I'd like to go back to the issue of the reports that went from the 35th Division to the 3rd Corps and further up about the situation of the prisoners of war. When we were shown, by Defence counsel, the reports of 25th July 1995 from the 3rd Corps back to the Supreme Command, it seemed as if an interview had, in fact, been -- a second interview had, in fact, been conducted by the 35th Division. I was puzzled by a remark that you gave -- a comment that you gave to that report because I think you said something in the meaning that you didn't know whether that interview had, in fact, ever taken place. Maybe I misunderstood you, but I just wanted to confirm if you were implying in any way that the report was fake.

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not what I wanted to say, but I really do not remember. That was such a long time ago, 12 years ago. I cannot recall anything in connection with that report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I realise that. The issue is whether you were aware of this second interview being made and that surprises me, and let the record show that you nodded negatively, your answer was "no." The issue is how a second interview could have taken place without you knowing. You were assistant commander of Security. I'm certain that you must have been informed about a second interview being made. If you simply can't remember, then that's fine, you just say so; but if you have any --

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, let's move a little further back in relation to the three Serbian prisoners who were taken by the El Mujahid Detachment, because you have testified that you actually had a chance to see these three gentlemen at a very brief occasion. I think it was on the 22nd of July in Livade, and you told us that they were very scared?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Was it your impression that they had been subjected to mistreatment?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have already said at that moment I, myself, was taken aback by the entire situation, and I really cannot remember all the details. I was under the strong -- I was strongly impressed by this entire event and especially by the guard who was standing behind me with his rifle, so that I cannot recall all the details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I accept that, Mr. Imamovic, but the issue at stake here is that somebody is now being accused of not ensuring that a possible violation of the rules was being properly prosecuted; and in order for prosecution to be initiated, someone would have to make the first note that mistreatment had taken place. So my question to you is, therefore, whether you were aware, when you met these people, that they had been subject to mistreatment. Did you see them? Did they have wounds or bruises that you could see?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of that, nor did I see anything of the kind. I don't even remember in what way they were tied, whether with hands in front or at their backs. The situation was tense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Did you at any point later on become aware of mistreatment of prisoners of war being held in detention by the El Mujahid Detachment or by the other El Mujahedin groups?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw anything of the kind, nor can I confirm that, but there were different rumours which actually were unverified stories, information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Imamovic, I have to ask you to be painfully precise here. You said you never saw anything, and I understand this to mean that you never saw any Mujahid combatant mistreating a prisoner. That, I accept, of course. But did you see any of the prisoners at this time or at any later time having signs of being mistreated?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall. No, I didn't see that. I had no occasion to see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What did you hear? What exactly were the rumours that you said you heard?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, mostly, these rumours, when the combat operations started in September 1995, referred to the fact that they were given a number of prisoners. And as I've already said, I never saw them and I did not know who had taken them prisoner, in what place, et cetera, apart from those that had been escorted to Zenica by the military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But did you hear of any mistreatment of prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing in particular, no particular mistreatment. Perhaps they were not treated fair, but I did not hear of any particular mistreatment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Were you in any way instructed or otherwise told not to raise the issue of possible mistreatment of prisoners of war being detained by the El Mujahid Detachment or other Mujahedin groups? Was there any understanding that this should not be included in your reports?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never received any such instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I know that you never received such an instruction on any formal level. My question was more soft: Was there any understanding that this was not to be passed on to the next level?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not warned of this in any way, nor did anyone impress it upon me, that that is the way things should be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Do you know if your superior in the security organ of the 35th Division, did he ever have a chance to see the prisoners of war at the Mujahedin camp?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What do you mean by you don't know that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he ever saw prisoners of war in the El Mujahedin unit's camp. I never talked about it with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But, sir, excuse me, the security organ was a small unit, as I recall. You were, what, four or five people in that unit, and it would appear to me to be strange if you didn't talk about what was happening.

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have occasion frequently to speak with my superior. The communication we had evolved mainly via reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But were you not sitting next-door to him? You were the assistant commander, and didn't your commander have his office just next to yours?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My superior in the security organ was in Zenica, and I was in Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Oh, I see. You see, what I'm trying to elicit is that despite the fact that there were rumours of prisoners of war being taken and possibly also rumours that they were being mistreated, it was all happening right under your nose and nobody discovered it. Nobody found it necessary to pass any of this information on to anywhere else, so nothing was ever reported on possible mistreatment. It surprises me that all the documents that we have seen on reports about these prisoners, these three prisoners and other prisoners taken by the El Mujahid Detachment or other El Mujahedin groups, in none of the reports do we find any reference to mistreatment being made, and I just wonder how that could be. Was there some sort of, as I said, understanding that this was not to be passed on, or was it accepted, but your answers to the questions that I've put to you is you didn't know about it, and so I guess I can't take it any further, unless you're able to clarify further.

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One can't say that this happened in the city of Zavidovici. In the town of Zavidovici where I was, the combat operations front was huge. It was a number of kilometres around Zavidovici, so that we couldn't be everywhere at all times. So there was a vast possibility for things to be hidden, for anything to be hidden in so large an area. Prohibiting members of the El Mujahid Detachment to access the area, or other groups of Afro-Asian origin, actually contributed to the fact that we could not obtain true information, and that is why I can only talk about what we saw with our own eyes or were able to verify then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: The interview that apparently was made with the three Serbian prisoners by the 35th Division, and of which we saw the report dated 25th July, would that have been an interview made by the intelligence unit of the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But if an interview would have been taken by the 35th Division of a prisoner of war and it wasn't your section, the security section, could it have been any other unit or section within the 35th Division than the intelligence unit?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It could have been from the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Okay. So you're suggesting that the interview might have taken -- might have been carried out by the 3rd Corps and not by the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting. It's just that I don't know. I can't recall that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, last week, on Thursday, at page 3967, starting at line 22, you were asked a quest question: "Now, did you also send a copy of the report to the commander of the 35th Division, in addition to sending it to the security organ of the 3rd Corps?" Your answer was: "From time to time. Mostly, it was just an informative report, but the commander of the 35th Division was informed through regular briefings or in other ways." My question to you is: When you said, "From time to time," are we to understand that you had no set procedure for reporting?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There existed procedures but the commander was there, and we informed him at briefings, talks, talking to him, depending on the event, whether it was of substantive importance or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What do you mean by, "From time to time"?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the need arose, and depending on whether it was the -- the event was of essential importance so that the commander would have to be informed in order to bring an adequate decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I find that inconsistent with what you say, inconsistent with the statement that there was a set procedure. If you're going to report only as the need arises, then there is no set procedure. I cannot understand these two side by side. Either you have a system of reporting which is regular, like we have been shown here during this trial, what are called daily combat reports or daily reports. And, of course, if there is nothing significant to report, then you report that, and there was nothing significant to report but you don't just keep quiet. If you say you report as the need arose, then there cannot be any standard procedure for reporting, and I want to get from you, sir, what took place on the ground.

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mainly, there existed procedures, which does not, however, mean that they were always observed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: These procedures were not always observed. Okay. You have just been saying, in response to a question by Judge Harhoff, that you heard rumours of prisoners of war being kept by the El Mudjahedin Detachment; am I right to say that? Is that the rumour you heard? Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with all due respect, this witness never mentioned having heard rumours of the El Mudjahedin Detachment saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's why I'm asking him to confirm if I'm right or I'm wrong. Sir, was I right or wrong? What rumour did you hear?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard rumours that there were prisoners. But as to who took them, at what place and time, this is -- we did not have that kind of information. We didn't hear anything about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. My question to you, then, is: Did you investigate those rumours?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the extent possible under the circumstances, we did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What did you do to investigate? Just tell us exactly what your investigations involved.

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my collaborators sought, through their collaborators who were in the field, in the units, to find out as much as possible, to gather as much information as possible about what had happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what were the results of those findings out or gathering of information? Can we get what are the reports?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left the area very soon after the commencement of the combat operations and I assumed a different duty, so that I do not know what the subsequent reports were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And who are these collaborators of yours who sought information, and from which collaborators did they seek this information?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My collaborators in the security organ is whom I meant, and there were -- they were three or four officers who cooperated in a certain way with members of the B and H Army who were in the units, who were on the ground, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But, sir, the reports of those collaborators should be there, whether or not you were there for a short while or whether or not you left shortly thereafter.

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether there exist any because I wasn't there. I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you show us any request that you made to your collaborators to investigate this, at least at the time of initiating the investigation? You were still there, according to what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which request you are referring to, but this was a regular activity of all the people in the terrain, in the field, to collect such information. There did not need to be a particular issued request to that effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, when you say you don't understand what I mean by "request," let me refer you to the question I asked you a little earlier. My question was: "What did you do to investigate? Just tell us exactly what your investigations involved." You said: "Well, my collaborators sought, through their collaborators who were in the field, in the units, to find out as much as possible." Now, by "request," I mean your initiation of the investigations. Obviously, my question was: What did you do to investigate? And you said your collaborators sought. You must have, then, initiated that investigation.

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the request itself, what to submit, all information about important security-related developments in the field. It's not like anybody was being asked to do something specific. They all knew what their jobs were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What surprises me is that your job was security, and you don't seem to remember anything that has to do with the security of prisoners of war. You hear rumours. There doesn't seem to be anything that is done to find out whether the rumours are fact or fiction. This is your prime responsibility.

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was just a single element in our job, and we had a lot of other things to do as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed, it may be a single element, but it is an important element, is it not?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed. Let's go to another topic. You just told, again, the Court a little earlier, when you were being asked by the Judge here, that you cannot remember whether the prisoners of war that you found in Livade were tied with their hands in front or at the back.
